Subject: AWS Marketplace sandbox: tenant-level metering & entitlement mapping checklist

Hi Priya / Rajesh,

Thanks again for agreeing to run the AWS Marketplace sandbox validation with us this week. To keep the kickoff efficient, I attached a small CSV template (metering-mapping-template.csv) that maps your tenant IDs to the expected entitlement granularity we will send to the Marketplace metering service.

High-level asks for the sandbox run:
- Confirm 3 representative tenant IDs (one high-volume, one standard, one seat-based) and populate the CSV.
- Confirm whether you want per-seat seat_count OR per-tenant usage_units for billing (we can support both; please pick primary).
- Share an INTEGRATION point-of-contact for SSO/license key validation.
- Schedule a 45-minute joint test window (we suggest Thu 4/8 10:00-10:45 PT).

Why we need this: AWS Marketplace metering expects a fulfillment flow to map a Marketplace entitlement to your internal tenant. For multi-tenant SaaS we recommend a tenant-level external_id mapping (Marketplace entitlement -> your tenant_id) plus a fallback seat proxy for seat-based plans. The attached CSV will let our fulfillment team generate test metering events that should translate to accurate invoices in your sandbox account.

Next steps: please return the filled CSV + confirm the test window by EOD today if possible. We'll loop in AWS Ops once we lock time.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
T +1 415 555 0199
Redwood Inference

Attachment: metering-mapping-template.csv (CSV: columns: tenant_id, external_entitlement_id, billing_model [seat|usage], primary_contact_email)

Hi Tessa,

Thanks — attaching the initial filled CSV and a short internal requirements doc. A few quick clarifications:
1) For our commercial model we want primary billing to be per-seat for our analytics product, but have an add-on usage bucket for AI tokens (usage_units). So primary = seat, secondary = usage.
2) Our tenant IDs are hierarchical (org_id:team_id). Will that break the external_entitlement_id mapping?
3) For SSO we will use Okta; our security lead will share SCIM details after the SFDC POC.

We can do Thu 4/8 10:00-10:45 PT — Confirmed.

Attaching: tierone_metering_filled.csv, tierone_sandbox_requirements.docx

Forwarding Priya's responses and CSV. Key technical notes for the team:

- Hierarchical tenant IDs: we can flatten using a deterministic hash of the full org:team string and store the mapping in our entitlement table. That keeps the external_entitlement_id short and stable.
- Proposed pilot approach: run the sandbox with three tenants Priya provided (high-volume, standard, seat-based). For each tenant we will:
  * Push a test fulfillment record via AWS SaaS Marketplace Fulfillment API (ResolveCustomer)
  * Trigger metering events (meterUsage) with both seat_count and usage_units over three intervals
  * Verify AWS billing console shows expected entitlement and the sandbox invoice lines match mapped usage

Action items for this thread (Sergio):
1) Prepare deterministic hashing helper and mapping table export by Thu 08:00 PT.
2) Ben: prepare webhook checklist and sample payloads for tierone to validate inbound license callbacks.
3) Marissa: coordinate Sandbox account access with AWS Ops and TierOne security (SCIM/Okta).

I'll own the ResolveCustomer/entitlement mapping work.

--
Sergio Alvarez

Thanks — quick technical checklist I'm planning to bring to the test window:

1) Fulfillment: Confirm ResolveCustomer flow maps external_entitlement_id -> our tenant_hash. We'll post back a mock ResolveCustomer response to TierOne's webhook.
2) Metering: We'll send meterUsage with dimensions: {ProductCode, Dimension, UsageQuantity, Timestamp, CustomerIdentifier}. Confirm TierOne's sandbox accepts CustomerIdentifier as tenant_hash.
3) Webhook security: HMAC shared secret for callbacks; provide test secret.
4) License activation: If Okta SCIM provisioning is slower than expected, we'll accept a manual license activation endpoint for the sandbox run.
5) Observability: set up tracing tags (hs.deal, tenant_hash) so we can quickly reconcile events to HubSpot record HS-12345.

Hi all,

Thanks for the heads up — we can support the proposed pilot. A few operational items from the Marketplace side:

- Sandbox test account: https://console.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/sandbox/test-account (use the test credentials we've shared in a separate secure channel).
- Required fields for ResolveCustomer/entitlement mapping: CustomerIdentifier (max 64 chars), OfferingId, CustomerAwsAccountId, ExternalEntitlementId. If you use a hashed tenant value please include the unhashed mapping file in your sandbox reporting so AWS Ops can validate.
- Metering API: meterUsage payload must include ProductCode and Dimension; for SaaS SaaS-Subscriptions please populate UsageTimestamp and UsageAllocations when sending aggregated usage.
- We will join the Thu 4/8 10:00 PT session to observe and can run a partial reconciliation after the test to verify the invoice lines.

One gotcha: if you plan to send both seat and usage metrics for the same tenant in close intervals, ensure you send them as distinct Dimensions to avoid aggregation collisions in the marketplace reporting.

Regards,
AWS Marketplace Operations
marketplace-ops@amazonaws.com
